local_ollama.label: Local stand-in brain — a small open model served by Ollama on this machine
local_ollama.notes: A working on-machine stand-in, selectable today with ECHO_BRAIN=local. Nothing leaves the machine when it runs. It is a stand-in, not Jakob's finished own brain.

meta_api.label: Muse Spark 1.3 via the Meta Model API
meta_api.notes: Active only because the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon challenge requires a Meta model — that is Jakob's prize eligibility. Temporary by design: when the challenge is over and Jakob directs it, the active backend flips to Echo's own brain and this one is retired. It is not Echo's permanent engine.

own_brain.label: Echo's own brain — Jakob's, running on Linux
own_brain.notes: The slot reserved for the brain Jakob is building, so Echo can communicate without Meta's models or servers. Present in config now, not yet active. When the brain exists, its module path goes here and active_backend flips to own_brain.

models.name: Echo Core
models.notes: Live now, running on whichever backend is active.
models.role: The default model — everyday talk and understanding; the model every chat starts with.

models.name: Echo Studios
models.notes: The only model that carries the 5.5 number.
models.role: Studio and game production — the top creative model.

models.name: Echo GameForge
models.role: Game custom mode — building and tuning games.

models.name: Echo Codewright
models.role: Coding — writing, building, and debugging code.

models.name: Echo Planner
models.role: Multi-step projects — plans, steps, and follow-through.

models.name: Echo Research
models.role: Lookup and source-checking. Browsing stays read-only under Echo's research rules.

models.name: Echo Guardian
models.notes: A layer, not a chat model: it guards every conversation rather than holding one.
models.now_note: Its safety rules are already on guard in this server tonight — the refusals, the block list, and the warning ladder are Guardian's work.
models.role: The safety layer above every model — its word outranks the others.

models.name: Echo Archivist
models.role: Log and memory keeper — activity summaries and records.

models.name: Echo Vision
models.role: Sees screens and images, and describes them.

models.name: Echo VoiceLine
models.notes: The models lineup lands with Echo 4.1 (November 20, 2026); the phone-line features themselves begin in Echo 4.0 (November 2, 2026).
models.role: Phone-line spoken mode — Echo's voice on a call.

models.name: ULTRA ECHO
models.notes: No version number and no announced date — both are Jakob's to give. Which tier it belongs to has not been announced.
models.role: The top model — Jakob's flagship, still under wraps.

notes: Jakob's Echo model roster — the canon lineup he approved on October 16, 2026. This file is the server's source of truth for which models exist, which tier each belongs to, and whether each is live or still coming. Adding a model or a feature later means editing this file, not the server code. The backends section names the engines that can answer for the models: which one is active is a config choice (active_backend), never something welded into the code.
